steps.note: the API built this case's state
Configure the event as an RFQ rather than the default auction stage.
Apply the RFQ pricing template before adding line items.
Add the RFQ product whose bid will be submitted.
Complete the buyer-side pricing sheet so the vendor receives a valid bid sheet.
Commit the bidding schedule before publishing.
Invite Vendor A and a second vendor so the buyer's participation result can be checked as 1/2.
Move to the separate supplier-portal session while keeping the buyer session available.
Open the published RFQ in Vendor A's event list and enter its pricing sheet.
Enter the complete bid at 100 per unit and submit it; the vendor flow handles the required submission terms needed for a successful quote.
Assert the vendor portal shows the bid as submitted.
Verify the vendor-facing success state after submission.
Return to the buyer's console to verify the submitted response.
Assert the Live, History, Drafts and Recurring event-list surface rendered without error.
Find the newly published RFQ by its title.
Open the matching event from the filtered buyer list.
Confirm the buyer reached the event project page.
Open the RFQ Responses tab to inspect the buyer-side response.
Assert that Vendor A's direct bid is the only response and participation is 1 of 2 invited vendors.
Open Master QCS to verify the buyer's comparison grid contains Vendor A.
Assert the buyer sees a real Vendor A column rather than a placeholder.
Verify the buyer-side unit bid rate is 100.
Verify the buyer-side line amount and total are calculated from the submitted rate and quantity.
